explanation: Phalke's silent film, released in Bombay in 1913, is usually counted as India's first full-length feature. Steamboat Willie arrived 15 years later, in 1928.

claims.text: Raja Harishchandra, by Dadasaheb Phalke, was released in Bombay in 1913.
Steamboat Willie, starring Mickey Mouse, was released in 1928.
Raja Harishchandra is usually regarded as India's first full-length feature film.

writerNotes: Mickey feels like the dawn of cinema to many players, which is the trap. Fifteen years apart. Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor; the schema's riskReason list has no only or counterintuitive, so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Arguing for Steamboat Willie: Mickey feels ancient, but Indian feature films began fifteen years earlier. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: pairs an Indian landmark with a US one, so neither side needs local knowledge. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 24 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json, no match. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: Shree Pundalik (1912) is sometimes called India's first feature, so the label names Phalke's film itself and the explanation says usually counted.
